shortdesc.ph: Sets the number of times the audio effect loops.
Sets the repeat count for the media resource.

section.p: Call this method to set the number of times the audio effect loops. After all loops complete, the SDK triggers the callback and reports the playback state as PLAYER_STATE_PLAYBACK_ALL_LOOPS_COMPLETED.

note.p: For on-demand playback, the SDK triggers when a playback iteration completes. If more repeats remain, it reports PLAYER_STATE_PLAYBACK_COMPLETED (5) and continues playback. After the final iteration, it reports PLAYER_STATE_PLAYBACK_ALL_LOOPS_COMPLETED (6).

If you do not call this method or set loopCount to 0, the media resource plays once and reports PLAYER_STATE_PLAYBACK_ALL_LOOPS_COMPLETED (6) when playback completes. Each iteration reports only one completion state.

section.title: On-demand playback scenarios
section.p: Only playback-completion and stop states are listed. Intermediate states such as opening and playing are omitted.

strow.stentry: Reports PLAYER_STATE_PLAYBACK_COMPLETED (5) after the first playback, then PLAYER_STATE_PLAYBACK_ALL_LOOPS_COMPLETED (6) after the second playback.
Reports PLAYER_STATE_PLAYBACK_COMPLETED (5) after each playback, then repeats.

plentry.pd:
The number of times the audio effect loops:
≥ 0: The number of times to play. For example, 0 means no loop, play once only; 1 means loop once, play twice in total.
-1: Loop the audio file infinitely.

The number of repeats after the initial playback:
≥ 0: The repeat count. The total number of playbacks is loopCount + 1. For example, 0 plays once without repeating; 1 repeats once, for two playbacks in total.
-1: Repeat the media resource indefinitely. Each playback iteration reports PLAYER_STATE_PLAYBACK_COMPLETED (5) when it completes.
